claim.pdf_says: Heading '14.6.2.4   Initial state of object data' - a fourth-level clause number, the same depth as 14.6.8.1 / 14.6.9.1, which the transcription renders at '###'.
claim.markdown_says: Line 23799: '## 14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data'
claim.why_it_matters: Heading depth is the transcription's only machine-readable encoding of clause nesting. At '##' this four-part clause sits at the same markdown level as its parent 14.6.2 and as three-part clauses like 14.6.3, so a generated table of contents or an outline fold shows it as a peer of its own parent.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. (1) NO TEXT IS MISSING. The heading is present verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23802 (the claim's line 23799 is off by three) as '## 14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data', preceded by an explicit anchor ''. The clause number, the title, and the wording all match the PDF exactly. The claimed 'missing-heading' kind is a misnomer: nothing is missing. (2) THE PDF ITSELF DRAWS NO DISTINCTION. I rendered page 569 at 300 dpi and measured the ink bounding boxes of both headings: '14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data' occupies rows 388-431 (44 px tall, left edge x=337) and '14.6.3 Explicit and implicit transfers of control' occupies rows 862-905 (44 px tall, left edge x=337). Identical font, identical weight, identical cap height to the pixel, identical left margin. ISO's house style uses ONE uniform bold heading format for every clause level, so there is no typographic fact in the PDF that the markdown's '##' contradicts. Markdown '#' depth is a transcription-side representation with no counterpart in the source; a discrepancy requires the two sources to disagree, and here they cannot. (3) THE STATED RATIONALE IS FACTUALLY WRONG. 'Heading depth is the transcription's only machine-readable encoding of clause nesting' is false twice over: the full dotted clause number '14.6.2.4' is present in the heading text and is trivially machine-parseable, and every heading additionally carries a generated anchor ('section-14-6-2-4') that encodes the complete path. A ToC generator has the nesting available regardless of '#' count. (4) THE CLAIMED BASELINE CONVENTION DOES NOT EXIST. The claim asserts four-part clauses are rendered '###' by citing 14.6.8.1 and 14.6.9.1. Those two are indeed '###', but the surrounding evidence shows there is no consistent rule to violate: 14.6.9.4 is '##' (line 24038); 14.6.2 - a THREE-part clause - is '##' (23715) while the three-part 14.6.1 is '###' (23691); and 14.6.2.3.2 (23759) and 14.6.2.3.3 (23790) are FIVE-part clauses rendered at '##', i.e. shallower than their own '###' parent 14.6.2.3 (23742). Heading levels in this transcription were assigned per page without global hierarchy context - note that the first heading after each page marker (14.6.2 on p.567, 14.6.2.3.2 on p.568, 14.6.2.4 on p.569) resets to '##'. (5) NOT A PAGE-569 DEFECT. This is a document-wide levelling artifact of the automated transcription, and page 569 is neither its worst nor a distinctive instance; the five-part 14.6.2.3.2/.3.3 children outranking their parent are strictly worse and went unmentioned. Filing it as a per-page PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy mischaracterizes both its cause and its scope. Nothing on page 569 is missing, reflowed away, misquoted, or changed in meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The heading '14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data' is present and verbatim correct at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23802 (not 23799), with its clause number intact and an explicit 'section-14-6-2-4' anchor. Page 569 of the PDF prints this heading in exactly the same font, weight, cap height (44 px @ 300 dpi) and left margin (x=337) as the three-part heading 14.6.3 below it, so the source encodes clause depth only in the dotted number - which the transcription preserves. The underlying observation, if it is to be logged at all, is a transcription-wide markdown heading-level normalization issue (levels were assigned per page without global context: 14.6.1 is '###' but 14.6.2 is '##'; the five-part 14.6.2.3.2 and 14.6.2.3.3 are '##' under a '###' parent; 14.6.9.4 is '##' while 14.6.8.1 and 14.6.9.1 are '###'). That is a cosmetic tooling cleanup against the whole file, not a content defect on page 569.
